fixes.what: Above 768px, where every <details> is forced open, hide the summary: add `@media (min-width:769px){html.site-ready .accordion__read[open] summary{display:none}}`. The JS comment already claims 'the summary is hidden there' but no CSS does it; desktop-2 shows 'READ MORE –' sitting above text that is already fully open.
fixes.why: A dead toggle label inside the hero-grade open panel reads as a UI leftover, not an editorial device.

fixes.what: Set the operational paragraph to `color:var(--stone);font-size:16px;line-height:24px` (keep .accordion__intro in parchment at 18px).
fixes.why: Seven lines of 18px bold parchment over the photo (desktop-2) flatten the hierarchy; one headline, one bright intro, the detail recedes, like .statement__sub already does.

fixes.what: Add `text-shadow:0 1px 12px rgba(27,34,30,.9)` (the same shadow .hero__line already carries) and nudge `bottom` to clear the densest foliage, e.g. `bottom:calc(24px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`.
fixes.why: On the phone hero the Persian tagline sits directly on painted leaves and fruit; the only Persian line on the first screen should read cleanly.

fixes.what: Give the light interludes a 2px gold rule top and bottom (`border-block:2px solid var(--gold)`), matching the pageband and footer rules.
fixes.why: Desktop-3 shows the parchment ending as a bare flat slab against night with nothing framing the seam; the rule is the brand's existing device and makes the interlude look placed, not pasted.

fixes.what: Either raise the radial gold glow to ~.10 and bias it upward (`ellipse at 50% 30%`) or delete it and the --glow modifier.
fixes.why: At 6% the glow is invisible in the teaser screenshot (desktop-1 bottom), so the band reads as a plain deep block and the device is dead weight.

fixes.what: Move the SCROLL cue above the canopy line on desktop (e.g. `bottom:calc(40vh + 24px)` capped) or drop it on desktop as already done on phones.
fixes.why: Desktop-0 shows the gold-less cue printed on top of the painted foliage at bottom-left, the one place the art should sit untouched.
